subject.title: [Bug]: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` env var not inherited by `claude-cli` backend subprocess in Docker

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicitly configured trusted Claude Code config root while continuing to reject ambient `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` inheritance?
rationale: The current behavior is an intentional shipped security boundary, while supporting a custom credential root changes which hooks, plugins, instructions, sessions, and authentication identity a managed subprocess may load.

options.title: Add Explicit Trusted Root
options.body: Add a plugin-owned opt-in config path, validate it, keep ambient inheritance blocked, and document the required Docker mounts and authentication flow.

options.title: Keep Default Root Only
options.body: Preserve the existing boundary and improve diagnostics and Docker documentation to require the persisted `/home/node/.claude` layout or an operator-owned wrapper.

options.title: Restore Ambient Inheritance
options.body: Let the gateway environment redirect Claude Code configuration, accepting the broader hook, plugin, and credential injection risk.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Trusted Root
recommendation.body: Add a plugin-owned opt-in config path, validate it, keep ambient inheritance blocked, and document the required Docker mounts and authentication flow.

likelyOwner.reason: The release history attributes the existing Claude CLI environment-isolation boundary to this person.
